key_insight: Delta-corrected shot reduction (DCSR) corrects finite-sample bias in VQE measurement allocation to stabilize convergence and bypass noise-induced optimization plateaus.
engineering_relevance: DCSR could reduce measurement overhead in near-term quantum simulation while preserving the statistical resolution needed for reliable optimization.
method: Extend variance-preserved shot reduction with analytical finite-sample corrections.
Use the multivariate delta method to derive higher-order bias corrections to the empirical reduction factor.
Incorporate higher-order moments, including skewness and kurtosis, to improve shot allocation stability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and numerical simulations showing faster convergence than standard VPSR across varied noise and resource regimes, with equal or lower cumulative measurement costs.
watch_item: Higher-order moment estimates may themselves be unstable with very few pilot shots; the abstract does not report hardware validation or quantitative gains.
paper_title: Delta-Corrected Shot Reduction for Bypassing Optimization Plateaus in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
